Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D deficiency was a significant independent predictor of depression in CKD patients, with higher odds of depression among those deficient.
Sentence: "Multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that vitamin D deficiency was a significant independent predictor of depression after adjusting for confounding factors (adjusted odds ratio, 6.15; 95% confidence interval, 2.02-8.75; P = 0.001)."
Measured as: depression (WHO CIDI-Short Form)
Population: 533 patients with chronic kidney disease from KNHANES V, VI (2010-2014), mean age 70.1 years
Intervention: Vitamin D deficiency (serum 25(OH)D3 ≤10 ng/mL), observational exposure
Comparator: Vitamin D sufficient CKD patients
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 533
baseline_vitamin_d_status: at_or_above_20_ng_ml

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: In the RCT, vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood, including depression.
Sentence: "The vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood and serum concentrations of BDNF."
Measured as: depression (mood status)
Population: Healthy subjects with inadequate serum vitamin C (<50 μmol/L), n = 46
Intervention: Vitamin C 500 mg twice a day for 4 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
